faq.a: Mouloud is associated with the Arabic form مَوْلُود, whose core sense is mouloud; born, newborn (amazigh form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Mouloud?
faq.a: Mouloud is associated with Arabic. Mouloud is the North African form of Arabic مَوْلُود (Mawlūd), meaning 'born, newborn'.
Yes — the underlying form مَوْلُود is Arabic.
Mouloud can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Mouloud should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Mawlūd is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Mouloud, mouloud. Script forms are مولود, مَوْلُود, मौलूद.

faq.q: Is Mouloud a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
